items.title: Gordon Lorraine — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: A friend of mine from California, Mary Clark, who was very big in the women’s movement... So the two of us agreed to go... Mary and I were the only two Americans there.

ctx.x: You just told them good. You talked off-mike about your trip to Russia. Can you tell us about that?

Oh, yeah. Well, that’s how I got to Vietnam, actually. I was invited to go to the Soviet... It was Soviet Union then, believe me. I had met a woman from the Soviet Mission to the United States, Madame...her name is in there... Madame... I loved her. She was a nice lady. Anyway, we had some conversations, nothing more than that, and I never saw her again. But one day, an invitation came to my home when I was living uptown... I was invited... Three people were invited from the Women’s Strike For Peace, our…

Anyway, through much manipulation and all kinds of arranging, we got permission. The Russians were not happy about this, by the way. They didn’t expect us to go to North Vietnam. They invited us THERE. They’re the hosts. Now what? We’re going to go leave them. But they were...they did it for us, and arranged visas and all kinds of red tape and white tape and yellow tape, and people... We made it step by step... Through China. We had to go all through China. That was fascinating, and we did that—and now you’ve got…
